name: Macfos Ltd
title: Macfos Ltd - 543787 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Macfos (Robu.in), an online electronics distributor, reports FY26 revenue of about INR312 cr, up ~67% like-for-like, with no capacity or capex signal; debt funds inventory and margin is the key watch item.

summary.headline: Macfos (Robu.in) FY26 revenue about INR312 crore; ex one-time INR71 crore bulk sale in H1 FY25, revenue up roughly 67% and PAT up roughly 105%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of roughly INR312 crore, EBITDA of about INR39 crore and PAT of INR25.65 crore. Excluding about INR71 crore of one-time bulk sales in H1 FY25, growth was roughly 67% in revenue, 103% in EBITDA and 105% in PAT. Management said demand from corporate, B2B and B2G buyers is robust, and that the H2 and FY26 data in the presentation had mismatches that will be corrected in a re-uploaded deck. Q&A covered ROBU 2.0 (proprietary products), margin expectations, debt and inventory, warehousing, and working capital, where several questions went unanswered.

financial_highlights.change: about 67% YoY growth excluding INR71 crore one-time bulk sales in H1 FY25
about 103% YoY growth on like-to-like basis
about 105% YoY growth on like-to-like basis
management says among best levels achieved; no YoY figure given
Q3 about INR6,000 per analyst; Q4 implied about INR7,300

financial_highlights.value: rose from about 2.5 to about 6 (per analyst reading)
financial_highlights.change: not confirmed by management; attributed mainly to component category

segments.name: Robu 1.0 (electronics distribution)
segments.commentary: Core distribution business described as the backbone; growing fast and management is conservative on manpower additions here. No segment revenue split given, as management has stopped disclosing B2B/B2C breakup.

segments.name: Robu 2.0 (own products)
segments.commentary: Three segments launched about two years ago: drones (best traction, retail, government and military), modules and sensors. Portfolio includes about 300 SmartElex modules priced INR100 to INR2,000, plus SimplyFly and ProRange lines. Management gives no revenue target and says it is not yet a material share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance for ROBU 2.0; management targets gross margin about 10 percentage points above the core distribution margin on own-brand products, expected over 3 to 4 years.

Management said ROBU 2.0 could lift overall margin by about 1 to 2 percentage points in the long run if it reaches about 10% of revenue (example: 5% of revenue at 10 pp extra margin adds about 0.5 pp).
No specific capex plan for warehousing this year ('not as of now'); management targets capacity 30-40% above current order processing, which it says is an annual goal.
Management says margin will face natural pressure as scale and competition rise; it aims to hold gross margin at current levels.
Working capital days rose about 20 days versus end of FY25; management has not explained the driver yet and will reply by email.
Management has no specific date for moving to the main board; it said it meets the 3-year listing requirement but gave no timeline.
capex_capacity: Warehousing and order processing capacity expanded in steps; the current setup was taken 4 to 5 years ago and was outgrown in 2 to 3 years.
Management said the own-brand investment is mainly team (about 20 to 25 people in product development across three to four brands, up from about 4 two years ago), not equipment or inventory.
Inventory funded mainly by debt; management said most borrowing converts to inventory and that the banking partner (7 to 8 years) is comfortable with the debt level.
Inventory rotation days are an internal KPI with a reduction target, but the figure was not disclosed.
Management said defence engagement is at low volume and value, with a decision expected in 2 years on whether Macfos is in or out of that business.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is robust, with more corporate customers and repeat purchases; website and app traffic, order volumes, AOV and retention are trending positive.
AOV rise was attributed to B2B and B2G customers spending year-end budgets in Q4, plus a broader product portfolio and some strategic decisions; management said it is normal seasonality.
Memory chip shortages raised prices of development boards and drone controllers; management said it will price opportunistically within supplier agreements and competitive limits.
Management said AI edge demand is growing only modestly; the company already sells Nvidia, Arduino and Raspberry Pi boards.
Management estimated the India market at about INR10,000 crore by 2030, based on an internal study with many caveats; no current TAM figure was given.
Management said most orders are served from inventory; 15-30 day lead times apply to some orders, and high-volume customers wait about a month.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AOV jump from about INR6,000 in Q3 to about INR7,300 in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B and B2G customers spend year-end budgets in Q4, so the jump is seasonal and normal. The analyst dropped off the line before the follow-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue target and margin uplift for ROBU 2.0 products?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue number was given; the target is about 10 pp above core gross margin, and ROBU 2.0 is still a small share of revenue. Management says it is not aligning the target with ROBU 1.0.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drone and defence engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: Macfos supplies low-value, low-volume drone products directly to defence, focusing on one or two SKUs. Management said there is no substantial revenue yet and the company will be either in or out of the business within 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAM and customer profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are hobby, education, research and engineering; management declined to give a revenue breakup. A 2030 India market estimate of about INR10,000 crore was given from an internal study, with caveats.

qa_highlights.question: How is debt funding growth and what is the D/E comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most debt converts into inventory, that the bank has been comfortable for 7 to 8 years, and that it sees no need for equity now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and why did it hold up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to accept lower margin to grow business in FY25, and that component categories have improved margins while adding some dead inventory. It expects competition to erode margin over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did average monthly visitors drop from about 891,000 in March to about 600,000 H2 average, and what is the 'unique visitor' change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the presentation changed the method from summing quarterly unique visitors to a full-year pull, which removes duplicates. It will re-upload the data next week in the old quarter-sum format and said internal growth metrics are up.

qa_highlights.question: Is warehousing capacity enough, and are there capex plans this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it always plans for 30 to 40% extra capacity and will 'take a leap of faith' at some point, but there is no capex planned for this year as of now.

risks_watch: Slow-moving and dead inventory increase, mainly from the component category; management said the delta is in that category, but the breakdown was not provided.
Working capital days up about 20 days from FY25 end; driver not explained in the call.
Debt-funded growth: management says debt converts to inventory, but leverage levels are rising.
Gross margin sustainability as scale and competition rise; management expects natural pressure.
Data disclosure issues: H2 order count typo, visitor methodology change and unique-customer data mismatch; corrected deck still pending.
Supplier advances and material-in-transit balance at 31 March, unquantified in the call.
Concentration on memory-linked hardware costs and pricing decisions amid chip shortages.
Defence drone opportunity is early-stage and small; management cautioned against excitement.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year numbers and growth, but cautious and vague on ROBU 2.0 revenue, the defence business, TAM, and the working capital and inventory questions, where several answers were deferred or declined.
key_quotes: For a fair comparison, we have excluded one-time bulk sales of roughly INR71 crores which was done in H1 of financial year 24-25.
So we are not giving any revenue numbers as of now for ROBU 2.0 because I think ROBU 1.0 itself is a huge revenue.
But I'll say proportionally kaafi kam rahega wo in long run even.

growth.why: No forward revenue guidance; management targets Robu 2.0 gross margin about 10 pp above core, over 3-4 years, with no revenue target and no specific capacity additions or orders behind it, and no warehousing capex planned 'as of now'.
